plan: This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is a dominant strategy, regardless of what other bidders do. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down. Bidding exactly my value of $48 maximizes my expected profit: I win whenever my value exceeds the highest competing bid, and I pay only that competing bid, capturing the full surplus optimally.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with 3 bidders. In such auctions, bidding truthfully (bidding exactly my value) is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than my value, while underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With no prior history to adjust from, I'll bid my true value of $38.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors. Bidding higher than my value risks winning at a price exceeding what the item is worth to me; bidding lower reduces my chance of winning without improving the price I'd pay if I win. Since payment is determined by the second-highest bid, my own bid only affects whether I win, not what I pay conditional on winning. Therefore, I should bid exactly $12, my private value.
